facts.text: Cedar Creek, Texas takes its name from the nearby creek, located about eleven miles west of Bastrop in west central Bastrop County.
The town’s roots trace back to 1832 when Addison Litton, a Missouri native, received a league of black prairie on both sides of the creek.
In 1852, Elisha Billingsley opened the first local post office, marking Cedar Creek’s growing importance as a community hub.
By 1855, a Presbyterian church had been organized, reflecting the early settlers’ commitment to faith and community life.
In May 1888, African American men Orange Weeks and Ike Wilson were elected as peace officers, a notable moment in the town’s civil history.
Cedar Creek Park was acquired by county officials in 2008 and later upgraded with funding from the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department and the Lower Colorado River Authority.
